answer.rationale: memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing for SMB segments) is least supported for sustainable long-term qualified revenue because: (1) it explicitly omits retention impact data—critical for sustainability claims—saying only 'no measurable harm' rather than positive retention outcomes; (2) price-based acquisition in SMB segments typically correlates with lower LTV and higher churn risk, not addressed; (3) promotional pricing trains price sensitivity rather than building durable value perception. memory_44 ranks highest because enterprise sales-assisted flows and demo-request quality directly correlate with deal size, retention predictability, and long-term customer value. memory_31 and memory_86 rank 4 because they improve foundational activation and time-to-value—both preconditions for sustainable revenue—but don't directly measure retention or expansion. memory_91 ranks 3 because in-product messaging improves engagement metrics but lacks evidence of downstream revenue sustainability or cohort retention. memory_57 ranks 3 because referral programs in established customers show qualified revenue addition, but established customers are already on the books; the sustainability of *new* referral-sourced cohorts is unstated.
